x_axis.note: angle of attack ticks 10 and 90 deg on the bottom frame; only used to confirm the markers sit at about 90 deg

y_axis.note: bottom frame at slip 0 and dashed line at slip 1

marker.identification: manual: markers at angle of attack about 90 deg (direct ascent) read by eye for each slope series and refined to the colour centroid; the 10 and 17.5 deg series have no 90 deg marker (Table 3.2: data collection failure, test failure)

extra_points.note: Sec 3.4.1: on the 25 deg slope (actual 25.3 deg, Table 3.2) longitudinal slip reached 100 percent at 90 deg angle of attack

meta.source_title: Analysis of Angle of Attack for Efficient Slope Ascent by Rovers (H. Inotsume, Master's thesis, 2016)
meta.figure_or_table: Figure 3.9 (slip at angle of attack about 90 deg) with Table 3.2 actual slopes; Sec 3.4.1 text
meta.vehicle: Scarab rover set to 400 kg, four rigid wheels, active suspension disabled (Table 3.1)
meta.preparation: SLOPE tilt bed 6 m by 4.5 m, 0.23 m deep, soil loosened and levelled before each test; slope measured by stereo plane fit
meta.comparability_note: x values are the actual slopes printed in Table 3.2 for the 90 deg runs; y digitised from markers (means over the run, error bars 1 SD not transcribed). Slip ratio s = 1 minus vx over vref (Eq. 3.1). GRC-1 is a manufactured lunar simulant with a wide grading, not dune sand; 400 kg rover with large smooth wheels at 1 g. Soil properties from Table 2.1 (loosened). load_per_wheel_N derived here as 400 kg times 9.81 divided by 4 wheels. The last point is text, not digitised.
